text:
Today, October 1, Virgin Islanders honor Contract Day.

After our ancestors took their freedom from chattel slavery in 1848, the Labor Act of 1849 created a new kind of bondage. Workers were bound to one plantation for a full year, with a day wage and restricted movement, able to change estates only on Contract Day. It was freedom in name only.

On October 1, 1878, when rumors of reform proved false, 30 years of frustration ignited the St. Croix Labor Rebellion, known to us as Fireburn. It was led by four women we revere as our Queens: Mary Thomas, Mathilda McBean, Susanna "Bottom Belly" Abrahamson, and Axeline "Queen Agnes" Salomon.

They demanded fair wages and the repeal of the Labor Act, and many paid with their lives. From their sacrifice came reforms that dismantled the labor system.

Today we honor our heritage and remember their courage. 🔥

I am horrified by these sickening allegations and equally disturbed by how they were grossly mishandled by Cornell’s leadership. It takes immense courage to come forward as a survivor, and the institution that is meant to protect and keep students safe, by all accounts, failed her miserably. 

I support the DA’s decision to reopen the criminal investigation, but the accountability cannot stop there. We need a thorough, independent inquiry into Cornell’s handling of this despicable crime and the university’s broken Title IX reporting process. Anyone found complicit in this grave miscarriage of justice must be held accountable. 

This moment also calls for a hard look at the moral rot of a culture that made these students and administrators feel comfortable turning a blind eye to such a heinous, violent crime against this young woman. We have to do better.
